blocks.text: After his time in New York, Clark moved west, where he continued to shape the Libertarian Party on a national scale. He was elected Vice-Chair of the Libertarian National Committee in 1972 and later served as State Chair of the Libertarian Party of California. In 1978, he made headlines running for Governor of California, earning 377,960 votes—5.46% of the vote—a record for a Libertarian gubernatorial candidate that still stands. Two years later, Clark carried the party’s banner as its 1980 presidential nominee alongside running mate David Koch, earning over 920,000 votes

blocks.text: Brooklyn, NY -- The Kings County Supreme Court ordered that Matthew Morgan of the Brooklyn Libertarian Party, and the Libertarian candidate for New York City Council District 39, be placed back on the ballot this week. Morgan was removed from the ballot by the Board of Elections in the City of New York in June due to a cover sheet error. Honorary Judge Lawrence Knipel found that the Board of Elections had erred in its decision to remove Morgan from the ballot for his defective cover sheet, and that he had shown substantial compliance with state election laws and had made no errors worthy of disqualification. Matthew Morgan will therefore be on the ballot for the November 4,
